plain.li: I'm {OFFICE} now. I'll try to do it properly.
I'm {OFFICE} now. Three people have already stopped me to tell me what needs doing.
They chose me as {OFFICE}. I've started a list of what needs doing, and it's already long.
[newcomer] I've barely learned where everything is, and they've made me {OFFICE}. I'll be asking a lot of questions.
I didn't expect to be made {OFFICE}. I'll do it as well as I can for as long as they want me.
I'm {OFFICE} now. I don't feel any different, but people already look at me differently.
Made {OFFICE} today. I'll start with the jobs nobody else wanted and go from there.
Everyone here already does a bit of everything. Now I'm {OFFICE} as well.
I keep trying to look like I know what a good {OFFICE} does.
I'm {OFFICE} now. I hope I can make things a little easier for people here.
They made me {OFFICE}. I'll have to talk to a lot more people than I'm used to.

warm.li: They picked me as {OFFICE}. I'll try to be fair to everyone, including the ones who didn't want me.

blunt.li: I'm {OFFICE} now. Somebody had to be.

cheerful.li: I'm {OFFICE} now, and I'm more pleased about it than I'll let on to the others.

gloomy.li: Made {OFFICE}. Every complaint in the colony will come to me now.

cold.li: I'm {OFFICE} now. The others will expect things of me, and I expect things of them.

plain.li: [loss] Losing someone close changes what matters. I've given up trying to {OLDGOAL}, and I want to {GOAL} instead.
[loss] After this loss, trying to {OLDGOAL} feels like it belongs to someone else. I'm going to {GOAL}.
[loss] I keep thinking about how little time anyone gets here. I'd rather {GOAL} than keep trying to {OLDGOAL}.
[loss] I've thought it over and decided: no more trying to {OLDGOAL}. I want to {GOAL}.
[loss] The people we've lost had plans of their own. I've dropped my plan to {OLDGOAL} and mean to {GOAL} while I can.
[loss] Grieving has made me think about what I really want. It isn't to {OLDGOAL} any more. It's to {GOAL}.
[downed] I was lying on the ground thinking I might not get up. I'm done trying to {OLDGOAL}. I want to {GOAL}.
[downed] Nearly dying makes you sort out what you want. I want to {GOAL}, not to {OLDGOAL}.
[downed] When I was down and couldn't get up, I wasn't thinking about how to {OLDGOAL}. Now I want to {GOAL}.
[downed] I came close to not making it. I've let go of trying to {OLDGOAL}, and I'm going to {GOAL}.
[downed] I nearly didn't get any more time at all. I'll use what I have to {GOAL}, not to {OLDGOAL}.

warm.li: [loss] I'd always meant to {OLDGOAL}. Since we lost one of our own, I want to {GOAL}, and to spend more time with the people here.

blunt.li: [downed] Nearly died. Changed my mind. I'm going to {GOAL}.

cheerful.li: [downed] I'm still here, which means I get to choose again, and I'm choosing to {GOAL}.

gloomy.li: [loss] Wanting to {OLDGOAL} seems pointless after this. I want to {GOAL} before something takes that away too.

cold.li: [downed] Being downed showed me how short my time might be. My aim now is to {GOAL}, and trying to {OLDGOAL} is dropped.

plain.li: I'm {NEW} now, not {OFFICE}. It's still work worth doing, and I'll do it.
Moved from {OFFICE} to {NEW}. I'd be lying if I said it didn't sting a little.
[old] Going from {OFFICE} to {NEW} at my age isn't the worst thing. There's less of it to carry.
They've made me {NEW}. Whoever is {OFFICE} now can come and ask me anything they need to know.
Maybe I wasn't the best {OFFICE}. I'll try to be a good {NEW}.
Being {NEW} instead of {OFFICE} means fewer people come to me with problems. I'm not sure yet how I feel about that.
I'm no longer {OFFICE}, and they've given me {NEW} instead. I'll keep my head down and do the job.
[trait:Jealous] Somebody else is {OFFICE} now and I'm {NEW}. I'll be watching how they do.
I'm still on the council, as {NEW} now rather than {OFFICE}. That counts for something.
Someone at the stores called me {TITLE} without thinking about it. That's when I knew the name had stuck.
[old] I've been called plenty of things over the years, and {TITLE} is one of the better ones.
I heard two of the others talking, and one of them called me {TITLE}. They didn't know I could hear.
[small] There aren't many of us, so a name like {TITLE} gets used every day.

warm.li: People say {TITLE} kindly when they say it. I'm grateful for that.
I'll try to keep earning the name {TITLE}. People seem to mean it.

blunt.li: So I'm {TITLE} now. Fine by me, as long as nobody expects speeches.
Everyone's calling me {TITLE}. I've done the work, so I'll take the name.

cheerful.li: I'm {TITLE} now, and I grin every time someone says it.
Somebody called me {TITLE} and I said thank you twice. I'll get used to it eventually.

gloomy.li: Being called {TITLE} is nice for now. People forget these things quickly.
They call me {TITLE}. I hope I don't do something soon that makes them stop.

cold.li: People call me {TITLE} now. It's useful to be known for something.
The name {TITLE} has stuck. I'll make sure it stays accurate.

plain.li: {OTHER_nameDef} and I stood together when it mattered. We hardly talked afterwards, and we didn't need to.
I watched {OTHER_nameDef}'s side in the fight and {OTHER_pronoun} watched mine. I'll stand next to {OTHER_objective} again if it comes to it.

warm.li: After the fight I made sure {OTHER_nameDef} was all right before I did anything else.
I'm glad it was {OTHER_nameDef} next to me in that fight. I felt safer for it.

blunt.li: {OTHER_nameDef} didn't run. Neither did I. That's enough for me.
Fought next to {OTHER_nameDef}. {OTHER_nameDef} can be trusted in a fight.

cheerful.li: {OTHER_nameDef} and I came through it together, and we're already joking about it.
With {OTHER_nameDef} beside me I was a lot less scared than I expected to be.

gloomy.li: {OTHER_nameDef} and I both made it through that fight. I hope we're both as lucky next time.
I keep going over the fight in my head. At least {OTHER_nameDef} was there.

cold.li: {OTHER_nameDef} did what needed doing in the fight, without being told. I'll want {OTHER_objective} beside me again.
I've noted who held steady in the fight. {OTHER_nameDef} was one of them.

plain.li: {OTHER_nameDef} and I talk every day now, about nothing much. I'd miss it if we stopped.
[old] At my age you don't expect to make new friends, but {OTHER_nameDef} and I have become close.

warm.li: {OTHER_nameDef} is a good friend to have. I'll try to be as good a friend back.
I've started looking for {OTHER_nameDef} when something good happens, so I can tell {OTHER_objective} first.

blunt.li: {OTHER_nameDef} is all right. More than all right, actually.
Me and {OTHER_nameDef}, friends. Didn't plan it, but there it is.

cheerful.li: {OTHER_nameDef} and I are proper friends now, and I'm very pleased about it.
{OTHER_nameDef} laughs at my jokes, even the bad ones. That's a friend.

gloomy.li: {OTHER_nameDef} is a real friend now. I worry about losing the people I care about, and now there's one more.
{OTHER_nameDef} and I get on well. I'd forgotten what that was like.

cold.li: {OTHER_nameDef} is reliable and good company. A friend worth having.
I count {OTHER_nameDef} as a friend now. I don't say that about many people.

plain.li: Year {YEARS} here. I walked round the whole colony and tried to remember what it looked like when I came.
[old] Another year here, {YEARS} in all. I'm glad I'm spending my old age with these people.
My anniversary here, year {YEARS}. A few people said something, and it meant more than I let on.
[grieving] It's my anniversary here, but I didn't feel much like marking it this year.
Year {YEARS}. I know this place better than anywhere I lived before.

warm.li: Year {YEARS} with these people. I'm lucky to have them.

blunt.li: Year {YEARS} done. There's work tomorrow, same as always.

cheerful.li: Year {YEARS}, and I'm still glad I came.

gloomy.li: Year {YEARS}. I've seen good people come and go here.

cold.li: Year {YEARS}. I've made myself useful here, and the colony knows it.

plain.li: Back home after {DAYS} away. Before anything else I want to check on my things.
Home after {DAYS}. Everyone will want to hear about the trip, and I'll be telling it for days.
[winter] Home after {DAYS} in the cold. I can't wait to be warm again.
[summer] Back after {DAYS} on hot, dusty roads. The first thing I want is a long drink of water.
Back after {DAYS}. I'm still catching up on what happened here while I was gone.

warm.li: Home after {DAYS}. It was good to see everyone's faces again.

blunt.li: Back after {DAYS}. Feet hurt. Glad to be home.

cheerful.li: Home after {DAYS}. I've missed everyone more than I expected to.

gloomy.li: Home after {DAYS}. The road was hard, and I'm glad it's over for now.

cold.li: Returned after {DAYS}. I'll tell the council what we saw on the way.
